- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via getBookTree (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getBookTree, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/book/:name/tree), getItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getItem, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:ns/:name; the bare tail of client method meta.getItem, bound to GET /meta/:type/:ns/:name), meta.getBookTree (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/book/:name/tree, selected by route anchor /meta/book/:name/tree), meta.getItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:ns/:name, selected by route anchor /meta/:type/:ns/:name; the route ledger binds it to GET /meta/:type/:ns/:name), /meta/:type/:ns/:name (route, a path literal in MetadataEndpointsConfigSchema))_

> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/metadata_endpoints.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a28a271e86a556b8757c031c959bf6e992a0c83` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dffbaadf5978bf1b09bf71b73aebad62b03042cc` — the merge of head `cc5adeb43b99478ca8c015e0d8d6456573e1c9bb` into base `6a28a271e86a556b8757c031c959bf6e992a0c83`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dffbaadf5978bf1b09bf71b73aebad62b03042cc && git checkout dffbaadf5978bf1b09bf71b73aebad62b03042cc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a28a271e86a556b8757c031c959bf6e992a0c83 cc5adeb43b99478ca8c015e0d8d6456573e1c9bb && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a28a271e86a556b8757c031c959bf6e992a0c83 && git merge --no-ff cc5adeb43b99478ca8c015e0d8d6456573e1c9bb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a28a271e86a556b8757c031c959bf6e992a0c83
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6a28a271e86a556b8757c031c959bf6e992a0c83` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cc5adeb43b99478ca8c015e0d8d6456573e1c9bb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/metadata_endpoints.json

PR #33312 for card #33085. Inputs read: the card body and its four comments (6850771234, 6880054551, 6880069048, 6880624366), the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` (merge-base `fd7b378c`, 4 files, +17 / -3), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read at the head sha, not reviewed: `packages/rest/src/rest-config-mount-table.pin.test.ts`, `packages/rest/src/meta-qualified-item-route.ts`, `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts`, `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`. `main` (`24f2f401`) has not touched any of the four diff files or the pin since the merge-base.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** The only hunk in `rest-server.zod.ts` is inside the string literal passed to `.describe()` on `metadata.endpoints.item`. The key stays `z.boolean().default(true)`; no key, type, default, refinement or export moves. Nothing an author could write before is refused now, and nothing new is accepted.
- **Published surface: description text only — right.** The describe string ships in the spec `dist` and in the generated reference row; `liveness/metadata_endpoints.json` ships through the spec `files[]`. Both change wording only.
- **Generated output agrees with its source — right.** The `item` row in `content/docs/references/api/rest-server.mdx` is the concatenated describe string, character for character. No other generated artefact carries the string in this diff, and the check-runs that would say otherwise (`Lint · docs & code guards`, `Build Docs`) have not concluded (see the gate note below).
- **`packages/rest/**` untouched — right.** The claim made it read-only; the file list holds no rest path.

Gate verdicts on the head, read at 2026-11-14T16:28Z: 45 check-runs, 14 `success`, 9 `skipped`, 22 `in_progress`, 0 failed. Concluded green and relevant here: `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. Still running, so NOT yet verdicts: `Type Check` (workspace, source gates, debt ledger, consumer gates), `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8, `Lint` (ESLint, repo and tooling gates, docs and code guards, CI/release/engine gates, both scoped jobs), `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Live E2E UI`. This record does not stand in for them: the landing check (every PR check green) is still owed when they conclude, and the dev's own NOT-MEASURED family `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is among what CI has yet to answer.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/33085-item-describe-qualified-read.md` declares `@objectstack/spec` patch. That matches what the diff publishes: description text in one shipped package, no accept-set or type change. A `skip-changeset` would have been wrong, since both edited spec files ship. No other package is touched, so no other bump is owed.

Clause-②: no — carried on both the PR body and the changeset, and correct: the diff neither widens nor narrows what the schema accepts, and it is not a `(narrowing)` declaration. `Metadata-protocol: none` is also correct; no protocol member is read or changed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in the os-dev-report (6880624366): empty. Nothing to answer.
- `deviations`: none against the order. The one surface amendment (the liveness row note) was requested before the commit and granted by the seat in 6880069048; the diff stays inside the amended surface.
- Branch is `claude/project-thread-bgvfrd` rather than `claude/issue-33085-*`: declared in the claim (6880054551) as a platform constraint of `mode:thread`. Accepted as declared.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: three class-b entries, all the same count drift outside this card's surface (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` `registerPerItemRoute` docblock "thirteen mounts"; the same file's normalized-config `maintenance` docblock missing `POST /_migrate-record-currency-codes`; `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/api-backend.json` saying thirteen in three places). I read the first at the head and it holds. Not reviewed here; the seat still owes filing them. The pin's own row comment (`[#27627] Thirteen: ...`, above the `metadata.endpoints.item` row) has the same stale count while its file header says FOURTEEN — outside the diff, worth adding to the same follow-up.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no separate author note.
- PR is a draft with no auto-merge armed; nothing to disarm.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts` (hits).** The contract this string answers to is the JSDoc directly above `endpoints`: each switch's `describe()` enumerates every mount it takes, and the radius is pinned route by route in the mount-table test. I counted both sides at the head.

- The pin row `metadata.endpoints.item` removes fourteen: `DELETE`, `GET`, `PUT /:type/:name`; `GET` `/audit`, `/diff`, `/history`, `/layers`, `/published`, `/references`; `GET /:type/:ns/:name`; `GET /app/:appId/bundle`; `GET /book/:name/tree`; `POST` `/publish`, `/rollback`.
- The new describe names fourteen: the three verbs on `/meta/:type/:name` (3), `/references` and `/layers` (5), the six history routes (11), the qualified read (12), the book tree (13), the bundle (14). The two sets are equal; nothing is named that the pin does not list.
- The mechanism clause, "which answers through the item read's own handler", is true of the code and is the actual reason the switch takes the route. `registerMetaItemReadRoutes` assigns `readItem` only inside `if (metadata.endpoints.item !== false)` and hands it back; `registerMetaQualifiedItemRoute` opens with `if (!readItem) return`. So the qualified route is not gated by `registerPerItemRoute` (unlike the bundle) but by the handler being absent, and the describe says exactly that rather than borrowing the bundle's "same per-item registrar" wording. I tried to break this by looking for a second mount of the path or an arm that survives the switch: the route ledger and `rest-server.ts` show one registration site, called once per base with the same `scope`, and the JSDoc above `endpoints` already covers the environment-scoped second copy for every route.
- Same-file prose: no other count of the per-item face exists in this file (no "thirteen"/"twelve" left), so the claim's "same-file prose with the same drift" has nothing further to fix.

Findings:

1. **nit** — the describe calls the route "the package-qualified by-name read". The one route pattern `GET /meta/:type/:ns/:name` also serves the `_env` arm (`GET /meta/:type/_env/:name`, the environment's own item), which is environment-qualified, not package-qualified; `meta-qualified-item-route.ts` calls the route "the qualified by-name read" for that reason. The route and the radius are named correctly, so an operator learns the right thing about what the switch removes; only the adjective is narrower than the route. Accepted deviation; "the qualified by-name read" would be exact if the string is next touched.

**`packages/spec/liveness/metadata_endpoints.json` (in the diff; the ledger row for the same key, enforced by the `Spec property liveness` check, concluded `success`).** Only the row's `note` changes; `status`, `evidence`, `producer` and the verification fields are untouched, which is right, since who reads the key did not change. "fourteen mounts" agrees with the pin, and both attributions hold: #27627 for the bundle (the pin's own comment), ADR-0150 D5 / #31691 for the qualified read (the pin's row comment and the route file header).

2. **nit** — the rewrite left the trailing clause "which is what the switch name has always promised" attached to the qualified read rather than to "the whole per-item face" it used to qualify. Read literally it says the switch name always promised the qualified read. Wording only; the count and the routes are right. Accepted deviation or fold into the follow-up that fixes the rest docblocks.

No must-fix and no should-fix. Nits alone end the round; neither is on a prose face, so fixing either here would move the head past this record.

The rest of the diff (the changeset prose and the regenerated mdx row) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-bgvfrd`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5mswnWm181XgYcCUag`

**VERDICT: PASS**
